author: luhring
body:
Adds new root command `wolfictl ls`. This command lists packages that are defined in the given directory.

(This command uses "advisory-command-style" auto-detection or specified via `-d <path/to/distro/directory>`.)

## Usage

```console
$ wolfictl ls
7zip
acl
acme.sh
aerospike
alpine-keys
alsa-lib
...
```

### Subpackages

Specify `-s`/`--subpackages` to include subpackages.

```console
$ wolfictl ls -s
7zip
7zip-doc
acl
acl-dev
libacl1
```

### Specific packages

Pass package names as args to select a specific package. This is operating on _parsed_ configurations, **so factors like `range` data are already considered.**

```console
$ wolfictl ls -s glibc
glibc
ld-linux
glibc-dev
...
glibc-locale-af
glibc-locale-agr
glibc-locale-ak
glibc-locale-am
glibc-locale-an
glibc-locale-anp
glibc-locale-ar
glibc-locale-as
glibc-locale-ast
glibc-locale-ayc
glibc-locale-az
glibc-locale-be
glibc-locale-bem
...
```

The command exits 1 if any specified package can't be found, so this can be used in scripting to check for the existence of a package.

```console
$ wolfictl ls some-new-package 2>/dev/null; echo $?
1
```

### Querying via templates

You can also use the `-f`/`--format` flag to pass in a literal [Go template](https://pkg.go.dev/text/template) as means of rendering data in a particular way, or querying for specific fields in the Melange configuration on a per-package basis.

E.g.: see what licenses are used:

```console
$ wolfictl ls -f '{{(index (.Package.Copyright) 0).License}}'
LGPL-2.0-only
LGPL-2.1-or-later AND GPL-2.0-or-later
GPL-3.0-only
AGPL-3.0-only
MIT
...
```

E.g. see how we're grabbing source code:

```console
$ wolfictl ls -f '{{(index (.Pipeline) 0).Uses}}'
fetch
fetch
git-checkout
git-checkout
fetch
fetch
...
```

author: baconpaul
body:
Cmake option PEGTL_NO_STD_FILESYSTEM will mean there is *no* implementation of std::filesystem selected at compile time. This will invariably lead to a broken PEGTL if you set it and use file operations, but it is intended to allow a configuration on systems without boost or std::filesystem, which don't need filesystem access but do want memory parsing. This allows taojson memory parsers to compile back to macOS 10.13, for instance.

See discussion in issue #347

author: dhirallin
body:
Hey I finally got around to adding a pawn promotion dialog so that players can promote to something other than queen.
I nicked an idea from chess.com of having the dialog appear over the promotion square, so the player can simply double click the promotion square to promote to a queen. 
Also added a 'Promote to Queen' option to the Settings so people can still auto-promote if they want.
This was a pain in the ass to get working with premove, but it seems to work now. 

Secondly, updated Jquery and bootstrap and popperjs properly, i.e. updated the bootstrap css file in play.html and
updated the version numbers in package.json which I forgot to do last time

Thirdly, I did some work on the tooltips, cause I thought it was annoying how the tooltips were staying up over the Forward and Back buttons so you couldn't click on them. So changed it that they only appear on hover now when on Desktop (but kept them the same on Mobile). Since you got rid of the banner up the top, there wasn't enough room for the tooltips to appear above the navigation buttons which is why they were appearing over neighbouring buttons etc. Also added the ability to change the tooltip placement depending on screen size, i.e. top on mobile, left/right on desktop.  Let me know if that looks ok.

author: domdomegg
body:
Improve a lot of our setup, including:

- Add [Turborepo](https://turbo.build/repo), to better manage our monorepo setup. This isn't fully optimized yet: I think there are definitely places where we could improve the explicitness of task dependencies and move them into Turborepo from the NPM scripts. We could also benefit from standardizing the input and output directories further.
- Add [cspell](https://cspell.org/) configuration, including recommending the extension. I struggle with spelling, and this helps keep things neat and easily-understandable (including to GPT-like / translation / other tools). I've also gone through and fixed a bunch of the spelling mistakes it found. I'm tempted to make this part of the CI check, but I suspect this will be more annoying than helpful.
- Moved around a lot of the docs, to reduce duplication between packages and make it easier for people to discover the docs relevant to them. Also added documentation on using Turborepo.
- Standardized ESLint configs (mostly), and fixed lint issues
- Ensured everything works smoothly in VS Code (e.g. TypeScript, ESLint)
- Updated CI to use NPM caching + Turborepo + Turborepo caching, so it completes faster

Things still to improve
- DynamoDB local: AWS seem to like making [unannounced breaking changes](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/76592141/aws-js-sdk-suddenly-throws-the-access-key-id-or-security-token-is-invalid), plus upstream [doesn't](https://github.com/99x/serverless-dynamodb-local/issues/297) [seem](https://github.com/99x/serverless-dynamodb-local/issues/294) [to](https://github.com/99x/dynamodb-localhost/issues/62) [maintain](https://github.com/99x/dynamodb-localhost/issues/83) [things](https://github.com/99x/dynamodb-localhost/issues/79). This has been the cause of multiple unexpected breakages over the last few months, and I have come to the point where I think it's worth making our own stable fork that protects us from this somewhat.
- [for later] Formatting: it would be good to get prettier set up and working
- [for later] MWA build: it would be nice to make this less hacky
- [for later] Tests: we might migrate to Vitest, given it seems less prone to weird babel problems and is faster, plus the migration path is pretty easy.

author: madroach
body:
**Type of change**
Bugfix

**Issue(s) closed**
On OpenBSD amd64 a warning is emitted during compilation about `__WORDSIZE` being undefined. `PRIuS` is then wrongly defined as `u`.

**Fix**
Define `PRIuS` as `PRIuPTR` if the latter is available.

**Possible regressions**
Since it falls back to the old behavior in case `PRIuPTR` is undefined I don't expect any regressions. It still won't help platforms having neither `__WORDSIZE` nor `PRIuPTR`.

# Thank you for contributing an eval! ♥️

🚨 Please make sure your PR follows these guidelines, **failure to follow the guidelines below will result in the PR being closed automatically**. Note that even if the criteria are met, that does not guarantee the PR will be merged nor GPT-4 access be granted. 🚨

**PLEASE READ THIS**:

In order for a PR to be merged, it must fail on GPT-4. We are aware that right now, users do not have access, so you will not be able to tell if the eval fails or not. Please run your eval with GPT-3.5-Turbo, but keep in mind as we run the eval, if GPT-4 gets higher than 90% on the eval, we will likely reject it since GPT-4 is already capable of completing the task.

We plan to roll out a way for users submitting evals to see the eval performance on GPT-4 soon. Stay tuned! Until then, you will not be able to see the eval performance on GPT-4. **Starting April 10, the minimum eval count is 15 samples, we hope this makes it easier to create and contribute evals.**

Also, please note that we're using **Git LFS** for storing the JSON files, so please make sure that you move the JSON file to Git LFS before submitting a PR. Details on how to use Git LFS are available [here](https://git-lfs.com).

## Eval details 📑

### Eval name

Understanding of explicit and implicit type conversions in C/C++

### Eval description

This evaluation is designed to assess the model's understanding of explicit and implicit type conversions in the C/C++ programming language. The evaluation works by asking the model to predict the sizes of various expressions, with the results compared against the correct sizes generated by a standard C/C++ compiler.

Type conversion rules in C/C++ can be complex. For instance, take the following expression:

```c
(float)0 + 1.0
```

The above expression evaluates as a `double` type because `(float)1` is promoted to `double` before the addition takes place. This behavior is outlined in the C/C++ standard. As a result, the size of the expression becomes `8` bytes. This is because the expression is essentially equivalent to:

```c
(double)(float)0 + 1.0
```

Through this evaluation, we aim to test the model's grasp of these rules and its ability to apply them correctly.

While humans can easily reason about the size of the expressions in this eval, the results can also be obtained by running the code through a C/C++ compiler as shown below:
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdint.h>

int main() {
    printf("(uint8_t)0,%lu\n", sizeof((uint8_t)0));
    printf("(uint16_t)0,%lu\n", sizeof((uint16_t)0));
    printf("(uint32_t)0,%lu\n", sizeof((uint32_t)0));
    printf("(uint64_t)0,%lu\n", sizeof((uint64_t)0));
    printf("(float)0,%lu\n", sizeof((float)0));
    printf("(double)0,%lu\n", sizeof((double)0));
    printf("(uint8_t)0 + 1,%lu\n", sizeof((uint8_t)0 + 1));
    printf("(uint16_t)0 + 1,%lu\n", sizeof((uint16_t)0 + 1));
    printf("(uint32_t)0 + 1,%lu\n", sizeof((uint32_t)0 + 1));
    printf("(uint64_t)0 + 1,%lu\n", sizeof((uint64_t)0 + 1));
    printf("(float)0 + 1,%lu\n", sizeof((float)0 + 1));
    printf("(double)0 + 1,%lu\n", sizeof((double)0 + 1));
    printf("(uint8_t)0 + 1.0,%lu\n", sizeof((uint8_t)0 + 1.0));
    printf("(uint16_t)0 + 1.0,%lu\n", sizeof((uint16_t)0 + 1.0));
    printf("(uint32_t)0 + 1.0,%lu\n", sizeof((uint32_t)0 + 1.0));
    printf("(uint64_t)0 + 1.0,%lu\n", sizeof((uint64_t)0 + 1.0));
    printf("(float)0 + 1.0,%lu\n", sizeof((float)0 + 1.0));
    printf("(double)0 + 1.0,%lu\n", sizeof((double)0 + 1.0));
    return 0;
}
```

### What makes this a useful eval?

ChatGPT is an essential tool utilized by many developers during their software development processes. As such, its understanding of code semantics plays a crucial role in providing valuable and accurate support to programmers.

C/C++ is among the most widely-used programming languages in the field of software development. Given its widespread use, mastering the type conversion rules of C/C++ is paramount for a tool like ChatGPT. This evaluation helps ensure that ChatGPT can accurately interpret and apply these rules, thus enabling it to offer better support to developers working with C/C++.
## Criteria for a good eval ✅

Below are some of the criteria we look for in a good eval. In general, we are seeking cases where the model does not do a good job despite being capable of generating a good response (note that there are some things large language models cannot do, so those would not make good evals).

Your eval should be:

- [x] Thematically consistent: The eval should be thematically consistent. We'd like to see a number of prompts all demonstrating some particular failure mode. For example, we can create an eval on cases where the model fails to reason about the physical world.
- [x] Contains failures where a human can do the task, but either GPT-4 or GPT-3.5-Turbo could not.
- [x] Includes good signal around what is the right behavior. This means either a correct answer for `Basic` evals or the `Fact` Model-graded eval, or an exhaustive rubric for evaluating answers for the `Criteria` Model-graded eval.
- [x] **Include at least 15 high-quality examples.**

If there is anything else that makes your eval worth including, please document it below.

### Unique eval value

> Insert what makes your eval high quality that was not mentioned above. (Not required)

## Eval structure 🏗️

Your eval should

- [x] Check that your data is in `evals/registry/data/{name}`
- [x] Check that your YAML is registered at `evals/registry/evals/{name}.yaml`
- [x] Ensure you have the right to use the data you submit via this eval

(For now, we will only be approving evals that use one of the existing eval classes. You may still write custom eval classes for your own cases, and we may consider merging them in the future.)

## Final checklist 👀

### Submission agreement

By contributing to Evals, you are agreeing to make your evaluation logic and data under the same MIT license as this repository. You must have adequate rights to upload any data used in an Eval. OpenAI reserves the right to use this data in future service improvements to our product. Contributions to OpenAI Evals will be subject to our usual Usage Policies (<https://platform.openai.com/docs/usage-policies>).

author: giladreich
body:
## Summary

This PR implements automatic generation of platform independent CMake Package Config files when building and installing Allegro library.

Additionally it simplifies the process of versioning by making cmake parse the version directly from the `base.h` header file. The reasons behind this explained in the commit messages.

## CMake Feedback

### CMake Minimum Version Requirement

Is there any particular reason why the project keeps compatibility with legacy cmake v3.0? This version is kind of absolute these days. Most toolchains not using it anymore, including Android Studio and some other legacy tools and Linux distros. As CMake evolved a lot ever since and many bug-fixes, ideally should be set to 3.18 unless it really breaks compatibility for some projects and it is reasonable to reason about.

### CMake Package Config Files

Note that Allegro can still be used within cmake using the existing `*.pc` pkg-config files:
```cmake
find_package(PkgConfig REQUIRED)
list(PREPEND CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH "$ENV{ALLEGRO5_SDK}")
pkg_check_modules(Allegro5 REQUIRED
  IMPORTED_TARGET GLOBAL
  allegro-5
  allegro_primitives-5
)
```

However, this is not the recommended way. This especially becomes problematic when using CMake's `PkgConfig` module, as this is not going to work on Windows off-the-shelf because it relies on `pkg-config` executable and generally have platform dependent behavior.
As I was working on creating CMake examples for importing Allegro into the project, I noticed with the way Allegro library is currently distributed is not going to make this process easy to make it work the same on all common platforms. I then started writing a `FindAllegro.cmake` module, but quickly realized this is a bad idea considering Allegro is a component based library and each component may have different build configurations, which will also be difficult to maintain. CMake recommended way is auto generating package config files using [CMakePackageConfigHelpers](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/module/CMakePackageConfigHelpers.html), hence I decided implementing it directly in the current cmake configurations of Allegro. Using CMake Package Config files allows one to easily import the library into their project:
```cmake
find_package(Allegro CONFIG REQUIRED PATHS "$ENV{ALLEGRO5_SDK}")
add_executable(${PROJECT_NAME} "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/main.cpp")
target_link_libraries(${PROJECT_NAME}
  PRIVATE
    Allegro::allegro
    Allegro::allegro_primitives
)
```
And the rest of the `Allegro::*` import targets will be defined and only be linked if one specify them in `target_link_libraries`. The advantage of this that the configurations behind the generated import targets is hidden from the consuming projects. Meaning that one can distribute Allegro libraries that were built for all configurations (Debug, Release, RelWithDebInfo, MinSizeRel, Profile) and cmake will help the consuming projects to decide which imported libraries to use depending on the current configurations.
As an example, if my project have the same code as above and I build now in Release mode, it will use the Release libraries of Allegro. If I switch to Debug, it will switch to Allegro Debug libraries. This in mind that the consuming project does not need to change its code or introduce complex checks based on `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE` or `$<CONFIG>` generator expression.

### Wrong Usage of CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE

Note that the current CMake configurations [assumes that `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE` should always be set](https://github.com/liballeg/allegro5/blob/db64a60fdb7219a6f73a3b51d1d099144fe065ca/CMakeLists.txt#L39-L46). This is wrong because there are also multi-config generators, such as Xcode, Visual Studio, Ninja Multi-Config etc. This means one cannot easily build and package the library for multiple configurations:
```bash
cmake --build . --config Debug
cmake --build . --config Release
cmake --build . --config RelWithDebInfo
cmake --build . --config Profile
```
unless they regenerate the configurations and then rebuild. Additionally [there is no need to set `CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES` variable](https://github.com/liballeg/allegro5/blob/db64a60fdb7219a6f73a3b51d1d099144fe065ca/CMakeLists.txt#L44-L46), since it will only be defined if the current cmake generator is a multi-config generator. Projects will often check against it in order to know if `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE` should be set or not. As of CMake v3.9 it is recommended to check against the new [global property `GENERATOR_IS_MULTI_CONFIG`](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/prop_gbl/GENERATOR_IS_MULTI_CONFIG.html).
The [Professional CMake Guide book -- 14.3. Custom Build Types && 14.4. Recommended Practices](https://crascit.com/professional-cmake/) highlights the usage of `CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES` when needing to add a custom configuration type, as the case of Allegro where it also supports profiling (`Porfile`). One would set properties per configurations, e.g. for GNU's gcc compiler:
```cmake
set(CMAKE_C_FLAGS_PROFILE "${CMAKE_C_FLAGS_PROFILE} -p" CACHE STRING "")
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_PROFILE "${CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_PROFILE} -p" CACHE STRING "")
set(CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS_PROFILE "${CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS_PROFILE} -p" CACHE STRING "")
set(CMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS_PROFILE "${CMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS_PROFILE} -p" CACHE STRING "")
set(CMAKE_MODULE_LINKER_FLAGS_PROFILE "${CMAKE_MODULE_LINKER_FLAGS_PROFILE} -p" CACHE STRING "")
```

I was holding back from introducing this change in this PR, as it requires more changes considering there are multiple `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE` checks in the cmake scripts that may require compilation on all supported platforms for testing purposes. However I can provide this proposal in a separate PR if there is interest for such change, as well as updating the minimum requirement for cmake that will help getting ride of unnecessary cmake policies and help simplify other cmake constructs.

Open to thoughts.

author: agilgur5
body:
## Summary

Add a section to Storage Classes briefly describing the default StorageClass
- I was looking to add this to the docs myself, but then saw that #15575 had added this section and went through a few review cycles but was never completed and merged
  - So initially based it off that, rebasing and addressing all the feedback therein ([these](https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/15575#discussion_r317714805) [two](https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/15575#pullrequestreview-279732022) points specifically). I ended up rewriting significant chunks as part of the feedback as well as after generally reviewing the [style guide](https://kubernetes.io/docs/contribute/style/style-guide/) and style of the existing doc, trying to more closely match those.

## Details

- the PVC docs reference this and there is an administrator guide on how to change this, but no section within the central Storage Classes document
  - this has made it a bit difficult to explain how a default StorageClass exists as the StorageClass docs themselves barely mention it
    - for new cluster admins I was teaching in particular, I wanted to make sure they were aware of the pitfall that I hit with kOps in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/34549#issuecomment-643501992, so the note about more than one default was particularly relevant (as well as how the [implemented fix](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/110559) [works](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/110559/files#diff-77fd84defc818b9e6010794bf87e0eece0960dfeff196e19b7d84da8de15ddffR67))
  - with a new section, this makes it very clear and links out to other existing docs on the topic

author: y21
body:
Fixes #11065 (which is actually two issues: an ICE and a false positive)

It now makes sure that the function call path points to a function-like item (and not e.g. a `const` like in the linked issue), so that calling `TyCtxt::fn_sig` later in the lint does not ICE (fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-clippy/issues/11065#issuecomment-1616836099).
It *also* makes sure that the expression is not part of a macro call (fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-clippy/issues/11065#issuecomment-1616919639). ~~I'm not sure if there's a better way to check this other than to walk the parent expr chain and see if any of them are expansions.~~ (edit: it doesn't do this anymore)


changelog: [`useless_conversion`]: fix ICE when call receiver is a non-fn item
changelog: [`useless_conversion`]: don't lint if argument is a macro argument (fixes a FP)

r? @llogiq (reviewed #10814, which introduced these issues)
